subject: Post-demo: FinOpt control-plane & private POC qualification

Subject: Thanks + follow-ups from today's demo

Jonas / Avery,

Thanks for the demo earlier — appreciate the crisp walkthrough. A few follow-ups from my side as we start to narrow options between Redwood and a couple of hyperscaler-managed inference paths (we're benchmarking against AWS Bedrock + SageMaker endpoints and Google Vertex AI). High level: the PM and infra leads want to validate whether a Redwood private deployment will meet our connectivity and isolation requirements before we commit to a POC.

Top questions:
- Control plane: can Redwood's control plane be deployed outside our VPC (managed) while the inference nodes are in our VPC? What's the exact network flow and which ports/IP ranges need whitelisting?
- Air-gapped feasibility: we have one environment that must be strictly air-gapped for regulated data. Is the on-prem packaged private deployment fully self-contained (no egress) and what parts require customer-managed secrets/KMS?
- Audit & keys: do you provide customer-controlled KMS (HSM/KMS) integrations for model encryption and request audit logs with per-request tracing?
- Comparison ask: for each of the above, can you call out specific differences vs. AWS/Google choices (e.g., control plane routing, VPC peering vs private link, required egress for health checks)? This will help our infra team prioritize tests.

I've attached our security questionnaire and a draft SOW for budgeting. Please send a concise next-steps list and the minimum tests we should run in an initial 2-week private POC.

Thanks,
Priya
Priya Menon
Head of AI Platforms | FinOpt Analytics

Hi Priya — thanks for the list and for sharing the questionnaire + SOW. Quick recap and proposed minimal test plan so your infra team can triage quickly. I've also looped Marissa (AM) and Karthik (solutions) to scope the POC and answer control-plane/network questions.

Recap of how Redwood private deployment options map to your asks (short):
- Control plane routing: two supported patterns — (A) Redwood-hosted control plane + customer private data plane (nodes in your VPC) using mutual TLS and outbound-only, whitelisted egress to our control-plane endpoints; (B) Customer-managed control plane (full VPC or on-prem install) where we provide the control-plane package and you keep all traffic internal. Pattern B is the recommended approach for regulated or air-gapped workloads.
- Networking specifics: for pattern A we document public egress IP ranges and allowlist ports (443 for mTLS + health checks, optional 8443 for admin). For pattern B there is zero egress requirement; control plane components communicate over internal subnets. We will provide a CIDR/port spreadsheet for your network team.
- Air-gapped: the on-prem package supports an offline installation. It requires local package mirrors and an offline license token (we ship a signed token). No external calls are needed after the initial license validation (which we can perform via secure courier if required).
- Keys & audit: we support customer-managed KMS integrations (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, GCP KMS) and HSM for key wrapping. Audit logs include per-request trace IDs, and we expose logs to a customer S3/GCS bucket or a syslog endpoint.

Proposed 2-week private POC (minimum tests) — please run these in priority order:
1) Network reachability test (pattern A): open limited egress to our control-plane pilot IPs and validate node registration + model pull (we'll provide IPs).
2) Zero-egress validation (pattern B-ish): deploy control plane locally in a dev subnet and demonstrate model load and inference with no outbound to public internet.
3) KMS integration: validate key wrapping/unwrapping flow using your KMS (we'll provide a small test image and scripts).
4) Audit/tracing check: generate workload and confirm logs arrive in your bucket with trace IDs that link to request payloads.

Next steps from Redwood: 1) Karthik will send a short network checklist + CIDR/port sheet by EOD; 2) Marissa will share a one-page POC SOW and pricing outline; 3) I'll set up a 30-min technical kickoff early next week with your infra/security leads.

Would you like us to include an offline license validation option in the POC SOW?

Best,
Jonas Weber

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>

Subject: Internal: network checklist + suggested tests for FinOpt POC

Team — putting the concrete network checklist and test commands here so we can send a single package to Priya. These are intentionally minimal and measurable.

Network checklist (pattern A: managed control plane + nodes in customer VPC):
- Allowlist outbound to: 52.34.120.0/24, 52.34.121.0/24 (control-plane pilot IPs) on port 443 (mTLS) and 8443 for admin UI (opt).
- DNS: nodes must resolve controlplane.redwood-inference.com -> pilot IPs; TTLs need to be low for failover tests.
- Health checks: node -> control plane heartbeat every 30s; ensure NAT timeouts >= 120s.

Zero-egress (pattern B / on-prem):
- Steps: install control-plane package in isolated subnet; run local package mirror (apt/rpm docker registry); verify model artifact pull from local mirror.
- Verify: strace/tcpdump shows no outbound SYN to public addresses after initial license validation window.

KMS test (script):
- We will provide: kms_wrap_test.py (Python 3.9) that generates test key, wraps via your KMS API, deploys a short inference job that requests encrypted weights, and verifies successful unwrap.
- Success criteria: inference latency within expected baseline, logs show key_id and wrap/unwarp events.

Audit/tracing:
- Provide: syslog endpoint or S3 ARN; we'll send example logs with trace_id format "finopt-<shortid>-<unix_ts>".

Deliverables to Priya:
- network_checklist_finopt.xlsx (CIDR + ports), kms_wrap_test.py, short-runbooks for offline install, and a 1-page POC SOW draft.

I'll attach the checklist and the test script links in the external email.

-Karthik
